summary.headline: BEL FY26 revenue rose 16% to INR27,480 crore with EBITDA margin at 30%; FY27 guidance is revenue growth above 15% and EBITDA margin above 28%.
summary.overview: BEL reported FY26 revenue from operations of INR27,480 crore (up 16%), PBT of INR8,075 crore (up 14%) and PAT of INR6,048 crore (up 14%), with EBITDA margin of 30% versus 29% in FY25. Order book stood at INR73,882 crore as on 1 April 2026, against FY26 order inflow of INR30,045 crore. Management said all FY26 guidance parameters were met. The call flagged QRSAM contract signing expected by June 2026 as the key near-term order event, with FY27 order inflow guided above INR55,000 crore.

segments.name: Defence electronics (about 90% of revenue, FY27 mix guidance)
segments.commentary: Management guides defence at 90% and non-defence at 10% of revenue for FY27, plus or minus 1%. Non-defence is currently 8-10% of turnover, targeted at 15-20% over time.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Exports are 4-5% of turnover, with a target of more than 10% over 4-5 years; near-term increase expected only 1-2%. Export order book is about USD96 million for this year and subsequent years.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth of more than 15%.
FY27 EBITDA margin of more than 28%.
FY27 order inflow expected above INR55,000 crore, including QRSAM.
FY27 R&D investment target of about INR2,200 crore.
FY27 capex target of more than INR1,200 crore, with 20%-plus growth; FY26 capex was about INR900 crore.
Defence to non-defence revenue mix of 90:10 (plus or minus 1%), with any change to be updated mid-year.
capex_capacity: FY26 capex was about INR900 crore; FY27 target is more than INR1,200 crore, with larger projects planned over three years at Palasamudram, Chitrakoot and Vellore, alongside Ghaziabad and Bangalore.
Management sees no capacity choking for the next 3-5 years, and continues adding capacity to avoid constraints over 10-15 years.

Computing infrastructure (CPU/GPU) already exists at CRL Ghaziabad, CRL Bangalore, the software SBU and PDIC; a separate high-performance computing facility is planned soon. Compute investment was INR100-plus crore over the last two years, with INR100-200 crore more in approval.
AMCA: BEL and L&T (consortium, L&T lead) expected to receive the RFP within about 15 to 45 days; investment will rise only after selection as successful bidder.
demand_pricing: QRSAM contract: management expects signing by end-June 2026, with a 5-10% chance of slipping to July and a worst case of one more month. First production model is due within 18 months of signing; margins are not yet quantified and are expected to be similar to existing business.

Submarine P-75I: BEL expects more than 50-60% of electronics content, with about six subsystems. Electronics are typically 25-30% of submarine value (plus or minus 5%). Execution is expected over about 5 years, aligned to MDL's schedule.

Order book breakdown: electronic fuses about INR4,300 crore (over 7 years), LRSAM about INR3,500 crore, LCA about INR3,200 crore, BMP-II upgrade about INR2,800 crore, Ashwini about INR2,460 crore, Mi-17 V5 EW about INR2,200 crore, spares and miscellaneous about INR2,500 crore.

Big-ticket pipeline for FY26-28 includes NGC corvette subsystems (about 50% expected this year), Shatrughat and Samghat EW, HAMMER, Shakti Phase IV and MFR-X naval radar. Management expects one or two items above INR20,000-25,000 crore in the next 2-3 years.
Data centre: current orders are a few hundred crore; an indigenous end-to-end solution with C-DAC could yield INR2,000-10,000 crore, with a first segment of INR1,000-5,000 crore.
Semiconductors are 17-19% of material cost and are fully imported today; management says price increases are absorbable and indigenisation will offset them.
Indigenous content is 80-85% on average, 90% for DRDO-driven products, and 55-65% for older TOT programs; semiconductors remain the main constraint.

qa_highlights.question: Will the submarine (P-75I) programme add to BEL's business, and how big is its electronics share?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said BEL would supply more than 50-60% of electronics, about 25-30% of submarine value is electronics (plus or minus 5%), and execution could take about 5 years.

qa_highlights.question: When will the QRSAM contract be signed and how soon will execution start?
qa_highlights.answer: Signing is expected before June-end 2026 (5-10% chance of slipping to July). First production model is due 18 months after signing; margins are too early to call.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a one-off in other expenses, which rose about 36% YoY?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said the rise reflects regular provisions tied to scale, such as performance warranty and LD-related items; total provisions as a percentage of sales were similar to FY25.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the cash flow and working capital changes, including receivables rising about 30 days?
qa_highlights.answer: Receivables rose because customer payments of about INR were delayed past the previous year-end and received in April-May 2026. Receivable days have been around 140-150 for four to five years. Management did not explain the low FY26 operating cash flow to EBITDA conversion.

qa_highlights.question: How much supply chain disruption came from the Middle East crisis?
qa_highlights.answer: Some LRSAM sub-components from the Middle East were delayed about 1-1.5 months, but management sees no major FY26 revenue impact.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for margins after the wage revision?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said guidance already reflects the wage revision due 1 January 2027, with some higher employee cost expected in Q4 FY27, and that the margin outlook is based on indigenisation and product mix.

risks_watch: QRSAM contract signing timing (June vs July 2026) and final pricing and advance terms, which drive FY27 order inflow.
Order book flat near INR74,000 crore against revenue of INR27,480 crore; FY27 growth above 15% depends on big-ticket orders arriving.
Operating cash flow conversion: management did not explain the low FY26 OCF/EBITDA ratio; receivables are high and customer advances fell relative to order inflow.
Wage revision from 1 January 2027 and higher employee costs could pressure the 28%-plus EBITDA margin guidance.
Export orders are uncertain; a 1-2 big-ticket export lead is in the pipeline, with timing hard to predict.
Semiconductor import dependence and the Middle East supply disruption.
summary.management_tone: Confident on FY26 delivery and FY27 guidance, but deferred several answers to the closing remarks. Management was cautious on export timing and on QRSAM terms, which it said were still under finalisation, and was vague on the operating cash flow conversion question.
key_quotes: So, we are retaining our revenue growth of more than 15%.
EBITDA margins will be more than 28%.
The order inflow we are expecting this year more than INR55,000 crores.
So, we are still fully optimistic that before June end, we may get this order.

adds.what: Larger capex projects at Palasamudram, Chitrakoot and Vellore over three years, alongside Ghaziabad and Bangalore (no specific capacity numbers given)
High-performance computing facility (compute infrastructure), planned soon; INR100-200 crore more in approval

growth.why: FY27 revenue growth guided above 15% (held), with FY26 order book of INR73,882 crore (flat) and FY27 order inflow guided above INR55,000 crore incl. QRSAM expected by June 2026; capex of INR1,200+ crore and no capacity choke seen for 3-5 years, but no specific new capacity numbers or timelines given.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: FY27 EBITDA margin guided above 28% versus 30% in FY26, so management is guiding a step-down, and the wage revision from 1 January 2027 adds higher employee cost in Q4 FY27; QRSAM margins not yet quantified and expected similar to existing business.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.when: FY27 to FY29, capex spread over three years
rows.why: FY27 capex target above INR1,200 crore versus about INR900 crore in FY26 (33%+ step-up), with larger projects at Palasamudram, Chitrakoot, Vellore, Ghaziabad and Bangalore, but no specific capacity numbers or commissioning dates given, and management sees no choking for 3-5 years.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Revenue growth above 15% guided for FY27 on FY26 revenue of INR27,480 crore (+16%), with order inflow of INR30,045 crore in FY26 against a target above INR55,000 crore for FY27.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation was not quantified and management says there is no choking for 3-5 years, so no near-term announcement is firmly signalled; the HPC facility (INR100-200 crore in approval) and AMCA investment (only after selection) are the main pending items.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 guidance of revenue growth above 15% was held, and order book of INR73,882 crore is flat against FY26 revenue of INR27,480 crore, so the outlook depends on big-ticket orders arriving rather than an upgrade.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Order book flat near INR74,000 crore, FY27 growth above 15% depends on QRSAM (signing by end-June 2026, with 5-10% slip risk to July) and orders above INR55,000 crore, and wage revision from 1 January 2027 could pressure the 28% margin floor.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: QRSAM first production model due within 18 months of signing, and a data centre solution (INR2,000-10,000 crore potential, first segment INR1,000-5,000 crore) is in development with C-DAC, but no firm launch dates.

rows.label: QRSAM contract signing by end-June 2026
rows.when: Q1 FY27 (by June 2026), 5-10% slip risk to July
rows.why: Management expects signing before June-end 2026 and the contract is a key driver of the FY27 order inflow target above INR55,000 crore; first production model due 18 months after signing.

rows.label: Receivables and operating cash flow conversion
rows.why: Receivable days rose about 30 days with around INR delayed payments received in April-May 2026, receivable days typically 140-150, and management did not explain low FY26 OCF/EBITDA conversion; customer advances fell to INR12,500 crore.

rows.label: NGC corvette subsystems and big-ticket pipeline
rows.when: FY27 (about 50% of NGC expected this year)
rows.why: Management expects one or two items above INR20,000-25,000 crore in the next 2-3 years, with NGC corvette subsystems about 50% expected this year, but timing is uncertain.

tone.note: Management was confident on FY26 delivery and FY27 revenue growth above 15%, but cautious on QRSAM terms and export timing and vague on the low operating cash flow conversion; analysts pressed on cash flow, receivables and order book stagnation.
